observations.statement: diastrephō (G1294) shows a settled-state-vs-active-verb split by morph: perfect passive participles ('twisted,' 'crooked and twisted') name a fixed condition of a whole generation or a body of teaching (Matt 17:17, Luke 9:41, Phil 2:15, Acts 20:30's 'twisted things'), while present active participles and an aorist infinitive name the ongoing or attempted act of corrupting someone else (Luke 23:2's 'misleading,' Acts 13:10's 'making crooked the straight paths,' Acts 13:8's 'seeking to turn the proconsul away').

phthora (G5356) spans two genuinely different registers with no lexical marker distinguishing them: ordinary biological perishability applied to the resurrection body ('what is sown is perishable,' 1 Cor 15:42, 15:50; 'things that all perish as they are used,' Col 2:22; creation's own 'bondage to corruption,' Rom 8:21 -- none of these are moral), and explicit moral depravity ('the corruption that is in the world because of sinful desire,' 2 Pet 1:4; 'slaves of corruption,' 2 Pet 2:19; reaping corruption from sowing to the flesh, Gal 6:8). The word covers mortality-in-general and moral-rot-specifically as one lexeme.

phthora at 2 Pet 2:12 uses the same root twice in one verse -- false teachers 'will also be destroyed in their destruction' -- a deliberate wordplay (their own corrupting influence becomes the instrument of their own ruin) rather than redundancy.
G6882 (diastrophē, 'perverseness') and G7946 (kataphthora, 'corruption') both have zero occurrences and empty meaning blocks. Earmarked; no further analysis possible.
G6882 and G7946 are included in cluster_strong for M10 but have no live span occurrences anywhere in the base data. Flagged for the spine/integrity process as a batch with H3891, H4893B, H8397 below.

alach (H0444) exclusively Niphal in all three occurrences -- 'become corrupt' (Ps 14:3, Ps 53:3, identical wording) and 'one who is abominable and corrupt' (Job 15:16) -- matching its own meaning block's exclusive definition '(Niphal) to be corrupt morally': this root's moral-corruption sense is grammatically only ever something a person BECOMES or IS, never an act performed on another.

hophekh (H2017) in its one occurrence -- 'you turn things upside down!' addressed to those who invert the potter/clay relationship (Isa 29:16) -- a rhetorical accusation of inverting a fixed created order, not a general moral-perversity statement.
H3891 (lazut, 'perversity, deviation, crookedness') has zero occurrences in the live span/verse data. Earmarked; no further analysis possible.

laphat (H3943) in all three occurrences is literal physical grasping or turning with no moral content: caravans literally 'turn aside' and get lost (Job 6:18), Ruth 'turned over' in sleep (Ruth 3:8), Samson 'grasped' the temple pillars (Judg 16:29).

laphat (H3943)'s three occurrences are all literal physical grasping/turning with zero moral content -- the same gloss-homonym pattern already found and moved to SUNDRY for chul (H2342J/K) and shazar (H7806): this strong was pulled into the 'twist/perversion' family purely on an English gloss match ('to twist'), not on attested moral usage. Flagged as a cluster_strong membership question, not resolved here -- on the verse evidence, this strong belongs with SUNDRY's off-topic-but-real-meaning group, not this family.

mutteh (H4297)'s one occurrence renders as 'injustice,' not 'perversion' -- 'the city full of injustice' (Ezek 9:9) -- grouped there with family D's injustice vocabulary in the English surface even though this is a separately-catalogued strong.
H4893B (mashechat, 'corruption (ritual)') has zero occurrences in the live span/verse data. Earmarked; no further analysis possible.

salaph (H5557) as active, agentive perversion/overthrow -- explicitly of bribery in its own meaning block, and the verses bear it out directly: 'a bribe... subverts the cause of those who are in the right' (Exod 23:8), 'you shall not pervert justice... a bribe subverts the cause of the righteous' (Deut 16:19), plus God's own overturning of the wicked/mighty as a distinct sense of the same root (Prov 21:12, Job 12:19, Prov 22:12's 'overthrows the words of the traitor,' Prov 13:6/19:3's sin/folly bringing a person to ruin).

avah (H5753A) splits by stem into a physical-anguish sense (Niphal 'bowed down'/'twisted mind,' Isa 21:3, Ps 38:6, Prov 12:8 -- describing physical or mental bending under distress or folly, not moral wrongdoing) and a moral-confession sense (Hiphil 'perverted their way,' Job 33:27, Jer 3:21 -- explicit self-indictment of having done wrong).

avah (H5753B, same root as H5753A, split by the cataloguer's sense-assignment not by the text) overwhelmingly in the fixed confession formula 'we have sinned and acted perversely and wickedly' (1 Kgs 8:47, 2 Chr 6:37 identical wording; Ps 106:6's 'committed iniquity... done wickedness'; Dan 9:5's expanded version), all Hiphil -- a liturgical/confessional set phrase, not independent descriptions.

avah (H5753B) as a Niphal person-descriptor -- Saul's insult 'son of a perverse, rebellious woman' (1 Sam 20:30) -- naming Jonathan's mother by a fixed derogatory character trait, and 2 Sam 19:19's Hiphil 'did wrong' as a specific act a servant seeks pardon for.

avat (H5791) as active Piel perversion of justice specifically, framed as a rhetorical question denying it of God -- 'will the Almighty pervert justice?' (Job 8:3, occurring twice in the same verse for 'justice' and 'the right'), 'the Almighty will not pervert justice' (Job 34:12), and God's own positive practice named the same way in reverse ('he brings the way of the wicked to ruin,' Ps 146:9) -- plus the explicit denial 'to subvert a man in his lawsuit, the LORD does not approve' (Lam 3:36).

avat at Job 19:6 -- 'God has put me in the wrong' -- Job's own accusation that God himself has perverted Job's case, the sharpest use of this root in the whole family: the sufferer accusing the deity of the very injustice the strong elsewhere insists God would never commit (contrast Job 34:12/8:3 above, from other speakers in the same book).

avat's remaining occurrences are non-moral or generically figurative: Ps 119:78's 'they have wronged me with falsehood' (Piel, an interpersonal complaint), Eccl 12:3's Pual 'the strong men are bent' (literal aging bodies, no moral content) and Eccl 1:15's Pual participle 'what is crooked cannot be made straight' (a philosophical generalization about the world's fixed limits, the closest thing in this family to a direct proverb-form statement of the crooked/straight figure).

aqal (H6127) in its one occurrence -- 'justice goes forth perverted' (Hab 1:4, Pual, passive) -- explicitly paired in the same verse with law being 'paralyzed' and 'the wicked surround the righteous,' naming a systemic breakdown of the justice system rather than one person's act.

aqash (H6140) splits cleanly by stem into three roles: Piel active-corrupting ('make crooked all that is straight,' Mic 3:9, of corrupt rulers), Qal-participle self-descriptive identity ('he who makes his ways crooked,' Prov 10:9, an active but self-directed sense), and Niphal passive state ('he who is crooked in his ways,' Prov 28:18, a settled condition rather than an act).

patal (H6617) shows a genuinely literal 'twist' core (Niphal 'wrestled,' Gen 30:8's Rachel-and-Leah rivalry naming) alongside a person-identity sense ('the wily,' Job 5:13's Niphal participle for scheming people) and a distinct reciprocal-justice idiom in Hithpael, applied to God himself: 'with the crooked you make yourself seem tortuous' (2 Sam 22:27, Ps 18:26 identical wording) -- God matching a person's own moral posture back to them, not perverting justice himself.

shechat (H7844, Aramaic) at Dan 2:9 describes the Chaldean wise men's own 'lying and corrupt words' -- deceptive speech under threat of death -- while its two occurrences at Dan 6:4 describe the deliberate SEARCH for fault in Daniel that finds none ('no ground for complaint or any fault... no error or fault was found in him') -- the same word naming both corrupt speech by the guilty and the explicit absence of fault in the innocent, within the same book.

sarakh (H8308) in its one occurrence -- Jeremiah's image of Israel as 'a restless young camel running here and there' (Jer 2:23) -- a literal-animal-behavior metaphor for aimless, undisciplined movement, applied to describe unfaithfulness without using any direct moral-perversion vocabulary in the immediate clause itself.
H8397 (tevel, 'confusion/perversion in sexual sin') has zero occurrences in the live span/verse data. Earmarked; no further analysis possible.

tahpukhah (H8419) applied specifically to SPEECH in 6 of its 9 occurrences -- 'perverted speech' (Prov 8:13, 2:12), 'a perverse tongue'/'the mouth of the wicked, what is perverse' (Prov 10:31, 10:32), 'perverted heart devises evil' (Prov 6:14), and dishonest scheming signaled by body language ('winks his eyes... purses his lips,' Prov 16:28, 16:30) -- this root's dominant register is corrupted communication specifically, not action in general.

tahpukhah's remaining occurrences apply it to a whole collective identity rather than speech -- 'a perverse generation, children in whom is no faithfulness' (Deut 32:20) and general 'strange things' the eyes will see under drunkenness (Prov 23:33) -- both distinct from the speech-focused majority above.

This family's genuine literal crooked/bent-body metaphor for moral perversion (already the #1680 finding) is now confirmed with morph evidence to be systematically stem-marked in Hebrew: Niphal/Pual passive-bent forms tend toward physical or settled-state senses, Piel/Hiphil active forms toward the act of perverting/corrupting another or oneself. Combined with family F's identical Niphal-contrite/Piel-destructive split for dakha, this is now a second root-family showing the same stem-marked valence pattern -- worth checking whether this is a general feature of Hebrew Piel/Niphal alternation this whole cluster's method should routinely check for, not a coincidence local to two roots.
